preconditions.description: Every line after the first contains exactly two integers representing a point's coordinates.

preconditions.expression: all(line.split()[0].isdigit() and line.split()[1].isdigit() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: All coordinates in the input are valid integers.
The first line is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^4) representing the number of points.

preconditions.expression: all(xi != xj or yi != yj for i in range(n) for j in range(i+1, n) for xi, yi in [stdin.splitlines()[i+1].split()] for xj, yj in [stdin.splitlines()[j+1].split()])
preconditions.description: All points in the input are distinct.

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is an integer m (n ≤ m ≤ 2·10^5) representing the number of points in the good superset.
Every line after the first contains exactly two integers representing a point's coordinates.

postconditions.expression: all(line.split()[0].isdigit() and line.split()[1].isdigit() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: All coordinates in the output are valid integers.

postconditions.expression: all(abs(int(x)) <= 10**9 and abs(int(y)) <= 10**9 for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]])
postconditions.description: The absolute value of all coordinates in the output does not exceed 10^9.

postconditions.expression: points := [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]]] and all((xi != xj or yi != yj) for i in range(m) for j in range(i+1, m) for xi, yi in [points[i]] for xj, yj in [points[j]])
postconditions.description: All points in the output are distinct.

postconditions.expression: input_points := [(int(x), int(y)) for x, y in [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]] and all(p in points for p in input_points)
postconditions.description: The output contains all points from the input set.

postconditions.expression: all(not (p1 != p2 and p1[0] != p2[0] and p1[1] != p2[1] and not any((p1[0] == x and p1[1] == y) or (p2[0] == x and p2[1] == y) or (min(p1[0], p2[0]) <= x <= max(p1[0], p2[0]) and min(p1[1], p2[1]) <= y <= max(p1[1], p2[1])) for x, y in points if (x, y) != p1 and (x, y) != p2)) for p1 in points for p2 in points if p1 != p2)
postconditions.description: For any two points in the output set, at least one of the three conditions holds: they share the same x-coordinate (horizontal line), same y-coordinate (vertical line), or the rectangle formed by them contains at least one other point in the set.
